findings.reason: the node may reuse the existing 120-second constant and pass every declared case while reopening the concurrent-launch window on exactly the placed lane the earlier sections were written for; the bound needs to be derived from the placement wait, or the in-flight reading needs the launching supervisor's own liveness, and the done-when needs a case for a launch that is old but demonstrably still running.
findings.text: §13 bounds the window it guards by "supervisor startup and placement" and then frees a reservation with no worker record once it is older than LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECONDS (reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py:55 = 120 s), so on the fleet's srun placement a launch still queued for a slot past 120 s loses its reservation and the in-flight refusal, which reads "whose reservation is still held", admits the second launch this section exists to refuse — and s13's only aged case fabricates a stale reservation, so no case in its done-when can detect the direction that matters

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §4's done-when and write paths name tests/test_a_live_session_refuses_a_second_worker.py, which does not exist, while §4's own landing followup names tests/test_resume_finds_unrecorded_live_session.py, which does; and every commit sha the plan cites (a88e6f09, a4ef5f35b1, f4aa6c7dc6, 9587a26dd7, 70cde9ede3, e8c4677a43, abd5eca84c, 5bc89fc029) resolves, as do both evidence-archive fragments.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every repair section from s4 to s13 states a done-when and names at least one negative control (s13 declares four, each tied to a numbered case), and the two sections without one are read-only investigations s1 and s2, whose outcome is a named launcher rather than a guard.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs are required under the run directory with a revision header and a bare EXIT= line in every section from s9 to s13, and s13's real-home guard lists the operator's crew home with sizes and mtimes rather than asserting it stays untouched.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the write paths and the symbols the plan introduces are named by mechanism (_retired_attempt_ended, _launch_refused_by, _refuse_a_live_worker_before_the_worktree, tests/test_a_concurrent_launch_is_refused.py), and no section id, plan label or version tag reaches a filename, symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §13 states that post-attempt.json in-flight time is "bounded by supervisor startup and placement" and then frees an unaccompanied reservation at an existing constant, LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECONDS, so its own stated bound is outside the window it relies on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s13 is one deliverable, a reservation that exactly one relaunch door holds and that frees by age, and each earlier section names one repair.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every declared edge resolves (plan-depends-on a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner exists; section waits s7→s6, s9→s8 and s10→s11 all name real sections, and the two edges §13 relies on, s10's pre-worktree check and s12's receipt read, are both landed and present in reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2534 and reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1970), and the one companion named only in prose (a-queued-request-is-checked-when-queued §5) carries no declared edge because nothing waits on it.
